meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – English common law heritage, inherited through the former New Zealand colonial administration, overlayered by statutory recognition of customary law (fa'a Samoa), particularly in respect of land and chiefly titles.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus), in force for Samoa since 13 December 2020
World Trade Organization accession (2012) and associated TRIMs commitments
Bilateral Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and the Nordic states (Denmark, Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden)
Regional AML/CFT cooperation arrangements through the Pacific Islands Forum and the Pacific Financial Technical Assistance Centre (PFTAC)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), including the provisions governing registered agents, the registered office, and maintenance of corporate registers; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (No. 25 of 2018, as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Rules and related practice guidelines implementing the FATF Recommendations. The 25% UBO detection threshold is the FATF-aligned standard applied by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit to International Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the principal account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and documented screening of every shareholder, director, officer, UBO, source of funds and connected party against: (i) Samoa FIU domestic lists and Central Bank of Samoa enforcement actions, (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the US OFAC SDN list, (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and (v) the UK HMT sanctions list. PEP determinations follow the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 definition, covering domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and close associates. Any hit triggers Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), re-piercing of beneficial ownership, source-of-wealth verification, approval by the registered agent's AML Compliance Officer, and re-screening at intervals of no more than 90 days during the entire pre-incorporation engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry, Business and IP Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; name-clearance filing for International Companies is effected through a licensed registered agent via the MCIL Companies Registry e-services portal of the Government of Samoa.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name of an International Company must be expressed in Roman/Latin alphabet characters. A parallel Chinese business name (中文商号) may be recorded in the memorandum as a secondary trading or business-style name to serve the traditional Chinese-market clientele, provided the legal name remains distinguishable under s. 13 of the International Companies Act 1987 and is not misleading or contrary to public policy. A Chinese-character-only legal name is not registrable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 business days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant, acting through its licensed registered agent, may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, annexing legal submissions, evidence of goodwill, and, where relevant, the prior written consent of the Minister or sector regulator for any sensitive token. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 21 business days. A further refusal may be challenged by way of judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa. If the 30-day reservation window lapses, a new name-clearance filing and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only where a fully licensed Samoan registered agent maintains the statutory registered office in Apia, receives service of process, retains the UBO file, statutory registers and accounting records, and operates as the AML/CFT gateway. A pure mailbox, tele-address, or agent-less arrangement is not accepted for a Medium-Risk Enhanced, licensed M&A advisory International Company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at approximately 25% within the first 24 months for a Medium-Risk Enhanced M&A advisory International Company whose principals are non-resident; the probability rises to 40–60% upon any PEP or sanctions name-match, adverse-media identifier, or Enhanced Due Diligence trigger. Unannounced inspections are conducted at the registered agent's premises by the Registrar of International Companies and the Central Bank of Samoa FIU without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) (No. 17 of 1987), particularly ss. 6-10 (incorporation and registration), s. 12 (company name), and ss. 94-97 (registered office and registered agent); read with the Companies Act 2001 for residual procedural principles.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1: Application for Incorporation of an International Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed. The International Company may be incorporated with nil or nominal paid-up capital, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required. The maximum authorized share capital must be stated in the memorandum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the memorandum of association subscribe for the number of shares set opposite their respective names and that the initial paid-up capital be acknowledged in the company's records. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the address filed with the Registrar of International Companies, care of the licensed International Company service provider. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed first directors, and [Name] is appointed Secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute advisory agreements, and do all things necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL e-Registry Online Portal or in-person counter, Apia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for the proposed International Company name. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing registered entity, and must end with a corporate designation acceptable under the International Companies Act 1987. Retain the reservation approval reference for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Certified identification documents of anticipated directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a new name reservation with a distinctive alternative; a written reconsideration request may be filed with the Registrar within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL-approved International Company registered agent or licensed corporate service provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, stating the objects, authorized share capital, share classes, director powers, and registered office clause. Arrange for subscriber signatures to be notarized or certified by an approved witness, and obtain signed consents from the proposed first directors and secretary.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act from each proposed director and secretary
Certified passport copies or equivalent identity proof of subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any constitutional provision, revise the memorandum or articles and re-submit the amended pages with a certified red-lined version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 through the registered agent together with the Memorandum and Articles, consents, name reservation approval, and a statutory declaration of compliance. Pay the prescribed filing fee and obtain an official receipt. The application must identify the Samoa registered office and the licensed registered agent.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Consents to act from first directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, address the Registrar's requisition in writing within 30 days with corrected documents. A refusal may be appealed to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, with payment through the Ministry of Finance Treasury account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the application passes statutory examination, pay the official state filing fee and any first-year annual license fee. The Registrar will endorse the memorandum and issue the Certificate of Incorporation and company registration number. Confirm the details of the certificate against the application.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copy of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the service standard, submit a written escalation to the Registrar and, after 10 business days, to the Chief Executive Officer of MCIL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Retention of Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL-licensed International Company registered agent in Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter into a registered agent agreement with a licensed service provider in Samoa. The registered agent will maintain the registered office, receive legal process, hold the statutory records physically or electronically, and file the registered office address with the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered agent to accept service
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the proposed registered office address, appoint an alternative MCIL-licensed agent and file the revised registered office notice without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Formalities and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors, company secretary, and the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates, enter subscribers in the register of members, and open a corporate bank account. File the initial return of directors and maintain the registers of directors, members, charges, and other statutory records required under the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory record is inconsistent, prepare corrective resolutions and re-file the amended notices with the Registrar within 14 days to restore full compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licenses Division, Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence for Management Consultancy and Cross-Border M&A Advisory Services (issued under the Businesses Act 1975 and applicable Business Licences Regulations).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA required for office-based management consultancy and M&A advisory operations; no prescribed activity threshold is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to advisory services in a standard office environment. If any physical fit-out or waste generation occurs, the company must comply with municipal wastewater and solid waste disposal standards, PUMA planning consent requirements, and Water Authority of Samoa discharge limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA); structural clearance under the Samoa National Building Code for the registered office premises; and workplace health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labour and Occupational Safety and Health Division.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR) of the Government of Samoa, established 2023 by merging the Inland Revenue Department and Samoa Customs Division; operational as the single national tax and customs administration. Official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; customs formalities administered through the ASYCUDA World single window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) with the Registrar of International Companies and Trusts at the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). No minimum paid-up capital is required; non-resident beneficial ownership is permitted. Step 2: Appoint a licensed offshore service provider in Samoa to maintain the registered office and file statutory documents. Step 3: Submit TIN application Form TIN-01 to the MfR via the online e-services portal or in person, attaching the certificate of incorporation, charter or articles, certificate of good standing, beneficial ownership declaration, board resolution appointing directors, passport copies and proof of residential address of shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and the MCIL annual licence fee receipt. Step 4: MfR issues a Tax Identification Number within 5–10 business days and records the company in the taxpayer register with the status 'Exempt International Company (Offshore)'. Step 5: No Samoa income tax, VAGST or payroll registration is triggered if the IC derives no Samoan-source income; the only recurring compliance obligation is the annual MCIL renewal licence fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the IC is a non-resident exempt entity under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) enjoying a 20-year statutory exemption from incorporation (renewable on application) in respect of all Samoan income tax on income derived outside Samoa, VAGST on offshore supplies, stamp duty on instruments relating to the IC, and exchange control approvals on offshore transactions. The exemption is absolute for the moratorium period and does not require a fiscal ruling; it coexists with Samoa's source-based territorial income tax system under which even resident companies are generally taxed only on Samoan-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box elections are not a feature of Samoan tax law. Available elections and boundary mechanisms: (a) 'Opt-in' conversion under the International Companies Act 1987, whereby the IC re-registers as a domestic company under the Companies Act 2006 and thereby forfeits the exemption, becoming taxable on Samoan-source income; (b) voluntary VAGST registration election if the IC wishes to recover input tax on local overheads despite having no taxable Samoan supplies — practically inadvisable because it imposes return filing and invoicing obligations; (c) branch/permanent establishment election if the IC establishes a fixed place of business in Samoa, bringing profits into the corporate income tax net at 27% plus final withholding taxes; (d) no hybrid mismatch or fiscal unity elections are available; the IC cannot be grouped with domestic taxpayers for tax purposes; (e) an IC may apply to MfR for an advance tax ruling confirming the scope of its exemption, but such ruling is optional and non-precedential.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act, as amended, effective 1994, administered under the Tax Administration Act 2012
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 200,000 per annum in taxable turnover for domestic suppliers. Non-resident suppliers of taxable goods delivered in Samoa or services performed in Samoa are registrable with no threshold and may be required to appoint a resident agent for VAGST purposes. An exempt IC that supplies only offshore advisory services to non-resident clients from outside Samoa has no Samoan VAGST nexus and no registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime exists in Samoa. MfR requires registered suppliers to issue a valid tax invoice within 21 days of supply and to retain accounting and invoicing records for six years. Customs export and import declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World electronic single-window environment. MfR is progressively digitising taxpayer services through its online e-services portal; electronic invoicing is voluntary, and system-to-system integration is permitted but not mandated. Digital fiscal stamps are not used in the VAGST system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAGST applies under the VAGST Act to: (i) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply under customs control; (ii) services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the benefit is wholly consumed outside Samoa, including professional services such as cross-border M&A advisory, financial consulting and due diligence; and (iii) services directly connected with exported goods. For the M&A advisory boutique (ISIC 7020), advisory mandates executed outside Samoa for non-resident clients are extra-territorial supplies, thus outside Samoan VAGST entirely, and the IC is treated as making no taxable supply. Export proceeds for both goods and services must be repatriated to a Samoa-licensed bank within 180 days of export or invoice date, and supported by inward remittance evidence. A VAGST-registered exporter claiming input credits must file monthly returns within 28 days of month-end and substantiate each zero-rated supply with the documentation bundle below.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via ASYCUDA World with customs endorsement of physical exit (export goods only)
Commercial invoice and signed advisory/services agreement identifying the non-resident counterparty and place of supply
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for goods; for services, time-stamped engagement deliverables, offshore workpapers and board minutes evidencing performance outside Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds into a Samoa-licensed bank account
VAGST zero-rating declaration (MfR Form VAT-02) with supporting evidence of the client's non-resident status and beneficial ownership
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR may audit zero-rated and exempt supplies within a 3-year assessment period, extended to 6 years where fraud or wilful misstatement is alleged. Unsubstantiated zero-rating is clawed back at 15% VAGST plus a late-payment penalty of 2% per month, compounded, and late-payment interest at the Central Bank of Samoa benchmark rate. Shortfall penalties escalate to 50% of the tax shortfall for failure to take reasonable care, 100% for intentional disregard, and 150% for fraudulent conduct. Criminal liability under the Tax Administration Act 2012 includes fines up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years for knowingly issuing false export certificates or falsified remittance records; directors and officers are jointly and severally liable, and an adverse finding triggers deregistration and forfeiture of any tax exemption certificate held by an International Company.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: WST is a semi-convertible currency subject to exchange control administered by the CBS. Current-account payments, including dividends and professional fees, are permitted if supported by valid documentary evidence and settled through an authorized dealer. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections, intercompany loans, and outward capital repatriation, require prior CBS approval or filing of the applicable exchange control form. Profit remittance for International Companies is not blocked by the IC regime but is subject to ongoing payment instructions, availability of underlying audited financial statements, tax clearance where applicable, and CBS compliance review. No unconditional legal right to unrestricted conversion exists; CBS reserves the power to refuse or condition remittances in cases of inconsistent declarations or unresolved compliance issues.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 90 days from the date of shipment (or the contractually due date if shorter) and received into an account with an authorized dealer. Unless a CBS-approved export retention facility is granted, 100% of repatriated export receipts must be surrendered to the authorized dealer in exchange for WST. For services-driven export revenue derived from cross-border M&A advisory fees, the same surrender obligation applies to the inbound success-fee wire, unless the fee is retained offshore with the prior written approval of the CBS under a specific retention exemption. Application for retention requires form CBS-ER/01, evidence of invoicing, and the underlying advisory agreement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Trust and Success Fee Collection Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low (restricted). Samoa has no dedicated electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime, and no offshore digital EMI may act as a bank account holder for a Samoan International Company unless separately licensed as a bank or authorized dealer. Global fintech rails such as Wise, Payoneer, and Mercury may be used only as invoicing and collection facilitators that eventually settle into a licensed Samoan bank account. The CBS will not recognize an offshore EMI as an authorized dealer for exchange control purposes, and any attempt to use an unlicensed EMI as the primary treasury conduit will fail AML due diligence and may trigger a statutory compliance filing obligation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a medium-risk enhanced AML profile associated with an M&A advisory boutique, at least two authorized signatories, including either a director or the ultimate beneficial owner, must appear physically at the selected licensed bank for the in-person KYC interview. Remote onboarding is not generally permitted for International Companies without pre-existing CBS-approved relationship or an express waiver issued by the bank's AML Compliance Officer. All physical attendance must be supported by original company documents, notarized proof of identity, a genuine business-profile questionnaire, and a source-of-wealth statement for any proposed capital escrow funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company registered in Samoa with no local staff and no physical Samoan office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed management services agreement with a licensed Samoa trustee/registered agent, a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and International Company Register extract, a board resolution appointing the Samoan registered agent as its process agent, and a detailed transactional narrative showing nexus to advisory services rendered to non-resident clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value success fee receivable to be funded from target-completion proceeds originating from SPVs in mixed fiduciary jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The executed M&A advisory/engagement letter, full-source-of-funds explanation from the payer's bank, latest consolidated audited financial statements of the payer, ownership/entity structural chart down to UBOs, and executed indemnity securing the bank against any third-party disputed funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires referencing multiple M&A targets or multiple payers funneling from common escrow settlement accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A schedule of underlying transactions showing each counterparty, jurisdiction of risk, deal date, fee basis, and bank references; UBO declaration; sanctions and adverse media checks; and certified copies of non-disclosure agreements showing commercial merit of the fee structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intent to use the account for rapid receive-and-disburse clearing without maintaining minimum retained balances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual treasury projection signed by a director, source-and-application-of-funds budget, a written anti-money-laundering policy, transaction monitoring commitment, and confirmation that no cash or bearer instruments will be used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or capital injection wires from foreign shareholders must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 using an authorized dealer bank in Samoa. The transfer should reference the CBS exchange-control purpose code appropriate to the transaction (typically 'equity capital' for non-resident direct investment). The receiving bank will require the capital remitter to provide a telefax or SWIFT confirmation of the underlying corporate resolution authorizing the injection, identification of the ultimate source of funds, and the bank statement of the remitting entity. Once credited, the capital must be booked to a designated Capital Escrow Account if it is intended for subsequent deal-disbursement under an M&A escrow arrangement. In all cases, the instruction must contain a clear narrative field identifying the IC company name, the nature of the transaction, and the corresponding contractual reference.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for M&A transaction milestones, seller consideration, or cross-border settlement fees must be initiated via SWIFT MT103 for each direct beneficiary. For larger escrow-motivated payments conditioned on closing conditions, a Commercial Letter of Credit subject to UCP600 may be issued by the Samoan authorized dealer bank or confirmed through a corresponding bank in the target jurisdiction. Interbank treasury movements should use SWIFT MT202. All outbound instructions must be supported by the advisory agreement, board resolution, CBS exchange-control forms where required, and an FX instruction indicating whether conversion to a designated foreign currency is needed. No cash counter-payment or split-payment structure is permitted without a prior AML unit approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore trade-backed forward FX contracts with an authorized dealer bank, limited to settled underlying current-account transactions and supported by documentary commercial evidence.
Onshore spot FX contracts through the interbank market or authorized dealers for immediate conversion of WST to USD, AUD, NZD, or EUR.
Currency swaps approved by the Central Bank of Samoa on a case-by-case basis for bona fide foreign direct investment or cross-border M&A financing where natural hedge cannot be achieved commercially.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Fee (International Company Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May (or the last day of the incorporation anniversary month, as prescribed by regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee; continued default beyond 30 days exposes the company to administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return Confirmation (Registered Agent Annual Certification of Registers and Beneficial Ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies via licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of up to USD 500 per month; registered agent resignation may trigger automatic discontinuation and restoration costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applicable to a standard International Company; mandatory independent audit arises only when required by shareholders, a court order, or a supervisory license condition (e.g. banking, insurance, or trust activity under Financial Services Authority oversight).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 1987; no statutory obligation to file financial statements; records must be kept sufficient to reflect transactions and financial position, and may be maintained under IFRS or another recognized standard adopted by the board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each International Company, through its licensed registered agent, must maintain a register of beneficial owners and submit an annual confirmation to the Registrar as part of the renewal process; any shareholding or ownership change must be updated in the register and notified to the registered agent, with the annual confirmation capturing the position as at the anniversary date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 if a voluntary certified audit is engaged; otherwise USD 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard corporate income tax rate (International Companies are exempt from this rate on offshore income under s.168 International Companies Act 1987; the rate applies only if prohibited local business is carried on)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective Samoan income tax rate for a compliant International Company (IC) holding a current annual license and not generating Samoan-source income. Statutory exemptions cover income, capital gains, withholding tax and stamp duty; annual license fee replaces tax burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return (Form IC/AR-2024) under s.120 International Companies Act 1987 - filed electronically via the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFA) e-Registry portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days of the anniversary of incorporation; standard SIFA annual fee payment by no later than that date or, if the IC aligns to a calendar-year cycle, by 30 June.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, IC registration number and original incorporation date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact IC certificate name. A non-resident IC is not required to obtain a Samoan tax identification number unless it later files a taxable business return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of the registered office in Samoa and identity of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the office address in Apia maintained by the licensed agent; directors and shareholders may be non-residents and are not required to have a local address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full register of directors and shareholders, including beneficial ownership particulars required under SIFA guidance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List non-resident directors and legal entity shareholders; if nominee shares are used, append the identity of ultimate beneficial owners for AML-CFT compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration under s.168(2) of the International Companies Act 1987 that no business was conducted within Samoa during the reporting period and no Samoan-source income was derived.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must confirm the declaration truthfully; if Samoan advisory work has taken place, this box must be crossed out and the domestic CIT return must be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation and payment of the annual license fee, with confirmation of payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the fixed annual SIFA license fee (currently approximately WST 800/USD 300) by wire to the SIFA account. Penalties apply if payment is late.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IC Annual Return: initial late fee of WST 100 and WST 100 per month (or part) up to a maximum of WST 1,000; late annual license fee attracts a 10% surcharge. Persistent default leads to administrative strike-off/deregistration, loss of corporate veil protection and automatic revocation of tax exemption, with the former IC becoming taxable under the Income Tax Act 2012.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Company Income Tax Return (Form CT-1) - filed through the Ministry of Revenue online portal e-Revenue
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the fiscal year end (standard fiscal year is 31 December, so due by 30 June). An extension of up to 60 days may be approved by the Commissioner on written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business name, tax identification number, accounting period and country of tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an IC using this return because it has lost exemption, insert the SIFA registration number and the Samoa TIN; the non-resident IC is nevertheless treated as a Samoan resident for worldwide income if it is incorporated in Samoa unless a tax-treaty tie-breaker overrides.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Samoan-source income from advisory success fees, retainers, interest, royalties and other revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must report only Samoa-source income. Offshore M&A advisory fees are not Samoa-sourced if services are performed outside Samoa, but must be shown in a separate schedule if any exemption is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses directly incurred in producing Assessable Income, such as professional indemnity insurance, legal costs, travel for Samoan clients, and share of overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductions attributable to Samoan-source income are allowable. For a non-resident, apportionment on revenue or time basis is required; no deduction is allowed for expenses related to prohibited local trading without a business license.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 27% corporate rate, offset of tax credit for any foreign tax paid, and calculation of tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Samoan CIT is chargeable on offshore income of an IC; the computation must separate exempt offshore income. If a DTA applies, reduced-rate relief must be evidenced by a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of an authorised officer and electronic payment of the balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by bank transfer to the Ministry of Revenue account in Samoa. Instalment rules apply only to taxpayers with annual tax over WST 20,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a penalty of 5% of the tax due (minimum WST 500) plus interest at 1.5% per month or part-month on the outstanding balance. Failure to file after reminder is a strict liability offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 5,000 and imprisonment not exceeding two years; the tax, 100% penalty tax and personal assessment may be recovered as a debt.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions by an International Company to any shareholder, because s.168(2)(b) of the International Companies Act 1987 exempts dividends, interest and other sums paid by an IC from every Samoan tax and withholding tax. The ordinary domestic rate for dividends paid by a resident company to a non-resident shareholder is 15%, reduced to 5% where the recipient is a non-resident company holding at least 10% of the voting power.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No DTA relief is necessary for IC dividends, as the domestic exemption is self-executing. Where a taxable dividend or other Samoan-source payment occurs and a DTA (e.g. Australia, New Zealand, Norway) provides a lower rate, the payee must (i) obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate from the Ministry of Revenue (Form TRC-1, with annual fee of WST 100), (ii) submit an authorised Certificate of Residence from the treaty counterparty and a WHT relief declaration to the payer before the distribution date, and (iii) if excess tax was withheld, claim a refund within three years of the end of the calendar year under s.68 Income Tax Act 2012.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Samoa withholding rate is 10% for interest paid to a non-resident and 10% for patent/royalty consideration, except that no withholding applies where the payor is an International Company making a payment connected with its exempt operations. Under Samoa's double tax agreements, interest is generally limited to 10% and royalties to 5-10%, subject to submission of the TRC and beneficial-ownership declaration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No monetary Local File/Master File threshold is codified in Samoa. The Tax Administration Act 2012 empowers the Commissioner of Revenue to require contemporaneous pricing documentation for any related-party transaction where a Samoan taxable taxpayer is involved. A tax-exempt International Company is outside the scope of Samoan TP filing unless it is stripped of exemption; in that event the Commissioner may call for full documentation without any de-minimis threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies economic substance scrutiny through SIFA guidance issued under the International Companies Act 1987 in alignment with OECD BEPS Action 5. An International Company undertaking M&A advisory work must demonstrate (i) direction and management exercised in Samoa through resident-agent meetings and board resolutions, (ii) an active physical office in Apia, (iii) adequate local staff and operating expenditure commensurate with success-fee revenue, and (iv) an annual substance declaration to SIFA. A zero-substance or 'letterbox' IC risks withdrawal of IC status, and the entity can be re-characterised as a domestic taxable company liable at 27% plus 100% penalty tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company derives advisory success fees from Samoan clients (Samoan-source income) while filing the s.168 exemption declaration that no local business was carried on, and fails to file Form CT-1.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty tax equal to 100% of the tax evaded plus a further evader penalty of 50% of the evaded tax, and monthly interest at 1.5% until paid; upon conviction in court, a fine up to WST 50,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years under Income Tax Act 2012 ss.126-127.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or caused the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax and penalties, thereby piercing the corporate veil. The court may also issue a travel ban, a freezing order on personal bank accounts, a civil restitution order for the full amount of missing tax, and a custodial sentence of up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a physical M&A advisory office and closing deals physically inside Samoa through the International Company without the prescribed domestic business licence, or without converting the entity into a licensed Samoan company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 1987 s.184, fines up to WST 10,000 per day for continuing breach and mandatory strike-off/deregistration. All fees earned in the unlawful period become taxable Samoan-source income paid before tax clearance, and may be subject to a non-availability of exemption and a 100% denial of deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the daily fines and for the corporate income tax assessed on the illegal local trade, because they directed the IC to act beyond its lawful objects. The Registrar may apply for disqualification orders (up to 5 years) and a civil restitution order against the directors' personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to receive success fees from a sanctioned target, or laundering the proceeds of corruption through the IC's Samoan trust or bank account in connection with cross-border M&A deals, without conducting customer due diligence or making a suspicious-transaction report to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018, a body corporate is liable to a fine not exceeding WST 1,000,000, confiscation of the funds and ancillary property, revocation of the IC license, and publication of the penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML/CFT obligations apply to all officers personally. A negligent officer is liable to a fine of WST 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; a knowing breach carries imprisonment up to 10 years, a lifetime travel ban, and a restitution order for the laundered amount, with the corporate veil fully pierced to recover proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a shell with no physical office, no staff and no record of strategic management in Samoa, then falsely declaring annual substance to SIFA or submitting incorrect beneficial-ownership data, while claiming treaty benefits or an exemption on cross-border M&A fee income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under International Companies Act 1987 ss.196-198, a false declaration is an offence carrying a fine of up to WST 5,000 and deregistration; for tax purposes, the IC is re-characterised as a domestic resident company and is taxed at 27% with a 100% penalty tax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The misrepresentation is imputed to every director who certified it. Directors may be sued in civil restitution for all taxes evaded, barred from leaving Samoa, disqualified as directors of any Samoan company for up to 10 years, and, if convicted of perjury under the Crimes Act 2013, imprisoned for up to 7 years.
